latest_release.name: brename v2.15.0
latest_release.body:
- v2.15.0
    - flag `-N/--nature-sort` now applies to renaming as well as listing. [#36](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/issues/36)
    - fix: correct exclude-filter assignment and recursive filtering, handle explicit search paths and `--only-dir` consistently, and inspect metadata without reading file contents. Exclude-filter assignment fix by @mazkev. [#41](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/pull/41)
    - fix: validate normalized target names and conflicts, preserve symlink and `..` resolution, distinguish hard links, reject moving directories into their own descendants, and protect the working directory, its ancestors, dangling symlinks, and undo log paths during execution and rename preview. Add tests for native case-insensitive paths.
    - fix: deduplicate overlapping inputs before assigning numbers, reject number overflow, excessive padding, and cyclic dependencies, and order moves through directory aliases and link chains without changing move-chain or overwrite priority.
    - fix: check history writes before moving files, retain usable undo paths and completed operations after failures, preserve previous history when nothing changes, and escape special filenames while retaining compatibility with existing undo logs.
    - fix: reject malformed undo logs before moving files, prevent undo from overwriting existing paths, preserve failed and dependent operations for retry, including through directory symlinks, reserve recovery-log space before undo, and honor dry run and overlapping inputs when removing history.
    - fix: validate `{kv}` capture indices, support empty captures, use the corresponding key for each match, keep missing keys literally, and reject corrupt key-value input while stopping failed input commands.
    - fix: keep listing independent of rename and replacement checks, remove a data race in absolute-path listing, report output errors, and honor quiet mode while retaining errors and dry-run previews.
    - fix: add a timeout and HTTP-response checks to version queries, and avoid reporting older releases as upgrades.

detail.readme: # brename: batch renaming safely [![Built with GoLang](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered_by-go-6362c2.svg?style=flat)](https://golang.org) [![Cross-platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-any-ec2eb4.svg?style=flat)](#download) [![Latest Version](https://img.shields.io/github/release/shenwei356/brename.svg?style=flat?maxAge=86400)](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/releases) [![Github Releases](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/shenwei356/brename/latest/total.svg?maxAge=3600)](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/releases) `brename` is a cross-platform command-line tool for safely batch renaming files/directories via regular expressions. ## Table of Contents - [Features](#features) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples](#examples) - [Real-world examples](#real-world-examples) - [FAQS](#faqs) - [Contact](#contact) - [License](#license) - [Starchart](#starchart) ## Features - **Cross-platform**. Supports Windows, Mac OS X and Linux. - Windows file systems, including NTFS and FAT, are case-insensitive. Some operations are allowed on Linux, while they could be dangerous on Windows. [For example](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/issues/28), renaming `test.tar.gz` to `test.tar` will overwrite `TEST.tar`. `brename` (v2.13.0 and later versions) can handle these cases appropriately (`-w` and `-W`). - **Safe**. ***It helps you check for potential conflicts and errors before it's too late***. Some common conflicts and errors that might happen with commands like `mv` or `rename`: - `New path existed`: **Existing files might be overwritten, causing data loss**. - `Overwriting newly renamed path`. **Existing files might be overwritten, causing data loss.** This case is hard to check by eye. - `Missing target`: The new filename is empty, which is not allowed. - `New path ending with a space`: Not allowed in Windows. It's legal in Linux, but might cause unexpected errors. - `New path ending with a period`: Not allowed in Windows. - **Supporting dry runs**. A good habit. - **Supporting Undo** for the last rename operation, including completed moves from a failed run. - **Overwrites can be detected and users can choose whether to overwrite or skip them** (`-o/--overwrite-mode`). - **File filtering**. - Supports including (`-f/--include-filters`) and excluding (`-F/--exclude-filters`) files via regular expressions. - No need to run commands like `find ./ -name "*.html" -exec CMD`. - **Renaming submatches with corresponding values via a key-value file** (`-r "{kv}" -k kv.tsv`). - **Renaming via ascending integers** (`-r "{nr}"`). - **Automatically making directories**: e.g., renaming `a-b-c.txt` to `a/b/c.txt`. - **Recursively renaming both files and directories** (`-R/--recursive`, `-D/--including-dir`, `--only-dir`). ## Installation `brename` is implemented in the [Go](https://golang.org/) programming language; executable binary files **for most popular operating systems** are freely available on the [releases](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/releases) page. #### Method 0: Conda [Install conda](https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/install/index.html), then run conda install -c conda-forge brename Or use [mamba](https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation/mamba-installation.html), which is faster. mamba install -c conda-forge brename #### Method 1: Download binaries [brename v2.15.0](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/releases/tag/v2.15.0) [![Github Releases (by Release)](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/shenwei356/brename/v2.15.0/total.svg)](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/releases/tag/v2.15.0) ***Tip: run `brename -V` to check for updates!*** Version checks wait up to 30 seconds for GitHub and report network or HTTP errors. A release that differs from the installed version is shown as the latest release; it may be older than a local development build. Just [download](https://github.com/shenwei356/brename/releases) the compressed executable file for your operating system, and decompress it with the `tar -zxvf *.tar.gz` command or other tools. And then: 1. **For Linux-like systems** 1. If you have root privileges, simply copy it to `/usr/local/bin`: sudo cp brename /usr/local/bin/ 1. Or copy it to a directory listed in the environment variable `PATH`: mkdir -p $HOME/bin/; cp brename $HOME/bin/ 1. **For Windows**, just copy `brename.exe` to `C:\WINDOWS\system32`. #### Method 2: Homebrew brew install brename #### Method 3: For ArchLinux AUR users yaourt -S brename #### Method 4: For Scoop users scoop install brename #### Method 5: Compiling from source Go 1.26.0 or later is required. # download Go from https://go.dev/dl wget https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz tar -zxf go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz -C $HOME/ # or # echo "export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/go/bin" >> ~/.bashrc # source ~/.bashrc export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/go/bin git clone https://github.com/shenwei356/brename cd brename go build # or statically-linked binary CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags netgo -ldflags '-w -s' # or cross compile for other operating systems and architectures CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=openbsd GOARCH=amd64 go build -tags netgo -ldflags '-w -s' Run `sh packaging.sh` from the repository root to create release archives in `binaries/`, with MD5 checksums in `.tar.gz.md5.txt` files. The script builds amd64 and arm64 binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows. All builds and checksums finish in a temporary directory before release files are replaced. Build failures leave existing archives untouched. For development, run `go test ./...`. Case-insensitive path tests require a writable case-insensitive filesystem for temporary files. Set `TMPDIR` (`TMP` on Windows) to a directory on that filesystem, then run: ```sh go test -v -run 'TestCLICaseInsensitiveAliases|TestCLIForceUndoCaseInsensitiveParent' ./... ``` These tests report `SKIP` on a case-sensitive filesystem; a skipped case does not verify that behavior. Cross-compiling also does not run these filesystem checks. ## Usage ``` brename: a practical cross-platform command-line tool for safely batch renaming files/directories via regular expression Version: 2.15.1 Author: Wei Shen Homepage: https://github.com/shenwei356/brename Warnings: 1. The path in file systems like FAT32 or NTFS is case-insensitive, so you should switch on the flag -w/--case-insensitive-path to correctly check file overwrites. 2. The flag -w/--case-insensitive-path is switched on by default on Windows, please use -W/--case-sensitive-path to disable it if the file system is indeed case-sensitive. 3. After path normalization, new names ending with periods or spaces are not allowed. 4. Undo refuses to overwrite existing paths. Contents overwritten with -o 1 cannot be recovered. 5. Renaming the working directory or its ancestors, or moving a directory into itself, is not allowed. Search paths: 1. Overlapping inputs rename each source entry once; {nr} follows the first encounter. Empty path arguments are invalid; omit paths or use . for the current directory. 2. Moves finish before directory or symlink parents used by their paths are renamed, including link chains. Moves touching the same entry retain their original order. Cyclic dependencies are rejected. 3. -l lists matching source paths without reading key-value inputs or applying replacements. 4. Fatal search or target-check errors stop the scan with exit status 1 before any files are renamed. The error message states when not all paths were checked; -d does not suppress these errors. Three path filters: 1. -S/--skip-filters black list default value: ^\. (skipping paths starting with ".") 2. -F/--exclude-filters black list no default value 3. -f/--include-filters white list default value: . (anything) Notes: 1. Paths starting with "." are ignored by default, disable this with -S "". 2. These options support multiple values, e.g., -f ".html" -f ".htm". But ATTENTION: each comma in filters is treated as a separator of multiple filters. Please use double quotation marks for patterns containing comma, e.g., -p '"A{2,}"' 3. The three filters are performed in order of -S, -F, -f. 4. -F/--exclude-filters is prefered for excluding path, cause it has no default value. Setting -S/--skip-filters will overwrite its default value. 5. Skip and exclude filters also skip matching subdirectories during recursive search. Include filters select entries to rename without stopping traversal. Explicit search roots are searched. Undo and history: 1. Successful moves are recorded even if a later move fails. Undo failures remain in the log for retry. Malformed records are rejected before any undo move. 2. -U continues independent undo operations after failures and returns a nonzero status if any fail. Paths depending on a failed restore are skipped, including through directory symlinks. 3. -d previews renaming, undo, and --clear without changing files. Rename preview checks undo log paths; undo preview lists recorded operations. 4. History stays in .brename_detail.txt. Existing logs remain readable, and ordinary filenames retain the old record format. Logs with filenames requiring escaping need an updated build. Moves that invalidate their own directory alias use resolved paths in the log. 5. Undo prepares a temporary recovery log before moving files; its directory must be writable. Special replacement symbols: {nr} Ascending integer {kv} Corresponding value of the key (captured variable $n) by key-value file, n can be specified by flag -I/--key-capt-idx (default: 1). Each match uses its own key. If any key is missing, the whole filename is skipped unless -K/--keep-key or -m/--key-miss-repl supplies a fallback. -K keeps a missing key literally, including any '$' characters. Special cases of replacement string: *1. Capture variables should be in the format of '${1}' to reduce errors. a). If the capture variable is followed with space or other simple, it's OK: -r '$1 abc' b). If followed by numbers, characters, or underscore. That is ambiguous: -r '$1abc' actually refers to the variable '1abc', please use '${1}abc'. -r '$2_$1' actually refers to the variable '2_', please use '${2}_${1}'. 2. Want to replace with a charactor '$', a). If using '{kv}', you need use '$$$$' instead of a single '$': -r '{kv}' -k <(sed 's/\$/$$$$/' kv.txt) b). If not, use '$$'. e.g., adding '$' to all numbers: -p '(\d+)' -d -r '$$${1}' Usage: brename [flags] Examples: 1. dry run and showing potential dangerous operations (-d) brename -p "abc" -d 2. dry run and only show operations that will cause error (-v) brename -p "abc" -d -v 2 3. only renaming specific paths via include filters (-f) brename -p ":" -r "-" -f ".htm$" -f ".html$" 4. renaming all .jpeg files to .jpg in all subdirectories (-R) brename -p "\.jpeg" -r ".jpg" -R dir 5. using capture variables, e.g., $1, $2 ... brename -p "(a)" -r "\$1\$1" or brename -p "(a)" -r '$1$1' in Linux/Mac OS X 6. renaming directory too (-D) brename -p ":" -r "-" -R -D pdf-dirs 7. using key-value file (-k) brename -p "(.+)" -r "{kv}" -k kv.tsv 8. do not touch file extension (-e) brename -p ".+" -r "{nr}" -f .mkv -f .mp4 -e 9. only list paths that match pattern (-l) brename -i -f '.docx?$' -p . -R -l 10. undo the last rename operation; retain failed entries for retry (-u) brename -u 11. disable undo if you do not want to create .brename_detail.txt (-x) brename -p xxx -r yyy -x 12. clear/remove all .brename_detail.txt files (--clear) brename --clear -R 13. also operate on hidden files: empty -S (default: ^\.) brename -p xxx -r yyy -S "" More examples: https://github.com/shenwei356/brename Flags: -w, --case-insensitive-path the file system (e.g., FAT32 or NTFS) is case-insensitive. It's automatically swiched on on Windows -W, --case-sensitive-path believing that the file system is case-sensitive. Please use this to disable the flag -w/--case-insensitive-path, which is switched on by default on Windows --clear remove .brename_detail.txt files; use -R/--recursive to include subdirectories -x, --disable-undo do not create .brename_detail.txt file for undo -d, --dry-run preview rename, undo, or history removal without changing files -F, --exclude-filters strings exclude file filter(s) (regular expression, NOT wildcard). multiple values supported, e.g., -F ".html" -F ".htm", but ATTENTION: each comma in the filter is treated as the separator of multiple filters, please use double quotation marks for patterns containing comma, e.g., -p '"A{2,}"' -U, --force-undo continue undo after failures without overwriting existing paths -h, --help help for brename -i, --ignore-case ignore case of -p/--pattern, -f/--include-filters and -F/--exclude-filters -E, --ignore-err ignore directory reading errors -e, --ignore-ext ignore file extension. i.e., replacement does not change file extension -f, --include-filters strings include file filter(s) (regular expression, NOT wildcard). multiple values supported, e.g., -f ".html" -f ".htm", but ATTENTION: each comma in the filter is treated as the separator of multiple filters, please use double quotation marks for patterns containing comma, e.g., -p '"A{2,}"' (default [.]) -D, --including-dir rename directories -K, --keep-key keep the key as value when no value found for the key -I, --key-capt-idx int capture variable index of key (1-based) (default 1) -m, --key-miss-repl string replacement for key with no corresponding value -k, --kv-file string tab-delimited key-value file for replacing key with value when using "{kv}" in -r (--replacement) -l, --list only list paths that match pattern, without planning renames -a, --list-abs list absolute path, using along with -l/--list -s, --list-sep string separator for list of found paths (default "\n") --max-depth int maximum depth for recursive search or --clear (0 for no limit) -N, --nature-sort sort paths in nature order for renaming or listing --nr-width int minimum width for {nr} (1-1000000). e.g., format "1" as "001" with --nr-width 3 (default 1) --only-dir only rename directories -o, --overwrite-mode int overwrite mode (0 for reporting error, 1 for overwrite, 2 for not renaming) (default 0) -p, --pattern string search pattern (regular expression) -q, --quiet be quiet, do not show any information and warning -R, --recursive rename recursively -r, --replacement string replacement. capture variables supported. e.g. $1 or ${1} (prefered) represents the first submatch. ATTENTION: for *nix OS, use SINGLE quote NOT double quotes or use the \ escape character. Ascending integer is also supported by "{nr}" -S, --skip-filters strings skip file filter(s) (regular expression, NOT wildcard). multiple values supported, e.g., -S "^\." for skipping files starting with a dot, but ATTENTION: each comma in the filter is treated as the separator of multiple filters, please use double quotation marks for patterns containing comma, e.g., -p '"A{2,}"' (default [^\.]) -n, --start-num int starting number when using {nr} in replacement (default 1) -u, --undo undo the last rename operation; retain failed entries for retry -v, --verbose int verbose level (0 for all, 1 for warning, error and renamed files, 2 for only error and renamed files) (default 2) -V, --version print version information and check for update ``` ## Examples Take this directory as an example (run `generate-example-folder.sh` to generate it): $ sh generate-example-folder.sh example ├── abc │   ├── A.JPEG │   ├── B.HTM │   └── B.JPEG ├── a.html ├── a.jpeg └── b.jpeg # examples below were executed in directory: example cd example/ 1. Recursively renaming all `.jpeg` files to `.jpg` in all subdirectories (`-R/--recursive`). A dry run is performed first to check for errors (`-d/--dry-run`). $ brename -p "\.jpeg" -r ".jpg" -R -d Searching for paths to rename... [OK] example/a.jpeg -> example/a.jpg [OK] example/b.jpeg -> example/b.jpg 2 path(s) to be renamed $ brename -p "\.jpeg" -r ".jpg" -R Searching for paths to rename... Done searching. Renaming paths... [DONE] example/a.jpeg -> example/a.jpg [DONE] example/b.jpeg -> example/b.jpg 2 path(s) renamed in 0.001 seconds $ tree . ├── abc │   ├── A.JPEG │   ├── B.HTM │   └── B.JPEG ├── a.html ├── a.jpg └── b.jpg 1. **Undo** the last rename operation (`-u/--undo`, `-U/--force-undo`) $ brename -u Renaming paths back... [DONE] example/b.jpg -> example/b.jpeg [DONE] example/a.jpg -> example/a.jpeg 2 path(s) renamed back in 0.000 seconds Undo refuses to overwrite files created at their old names. If an operation fails, its record remains in the log so you can resolve the conflict and retry. `-U` continues independent operations after failures and returns a nonzero exit status if any operation fails. Dependent paths are skipped even through directory symlinks. It does not enable overwriting. Use `brename -u -d` to list recorded undo operations without changing files. `brename --clear -d -R` previews history removal. Undo cannot recover contents overwritten with `-o 1`. History remains in `.brename_detail.txt`. Existing logs are still readable, and ordinary filenames retain the old record format, which older versions can read. Only logs containing filenames that need escaping use a versioned format; these require an updated build. Temporary writes use `.brename_detail.txt.tmp-*` in the current working directory, beside `.brename_detail.txt`, and replace the history file only after writing succeeds. Undo prepares a complete temporary recovery log before moving files, then reuses it for any remaining records. If this preparation fails, no files are moved. The history directory must be writable and have room for the temporary log. Undo logs must be regular files and must not alias files being renamed. With undo enabled, targets cannot use `.brename_detail.txt` as a directory. Do not run concurrent rename operations against the same paths or history file. Disable undo if you do not want to create `.brename_detail.txt` (`-x`) $ brename -p xxx -r yyy -x Clear/remove all .brename_detail.txt files (`--clear`) $ brename --clear -R 1. Dry run, only showing operations that will cause errors (remove `-d` to rename). # default value of -v is 2 $ brename -p a -r b -R -D -d Searching for paths to rename... [OK] a.html -> b.html [new path existed] a.jpeg -> b.jpeg [OK] abc -> bbc 1 potential error(s) detected, please check $ brename -p a -r b -R -D Searching for paths to rename... Done searching. [new path existed] example/a.jpeg -> example/b.jpeg 1 potential error(s) detected, please check 1. Ignoring cases (`-i/--ignore-case`) $ brename -p "\.jpeg" -r ".jpg" -R -i Searching for paths to rename... Done searching. Renaming paths... [DONE] abc/A.JPEG -> abc/A.jpg [DONE] abc/B.JPEG -> abc/B.jpg 2 path(s) renamed in 0.000 seconds $ tree . ├── abc │   ├── A.jpg │   ├── B.HTM │   └── B.jpg ├── a.html ├── a.jpg └── b.jpg 1. Using capture variables, e.g., $1, $2 ... # or brename -p "(a)" -r '$1$1' in Linux/Mac OS X $ brename -p "(a)" -r "\$1\$1" -i Searching for paths to rename... Done searching. Renaming paths... [DONE] a.html -> aa.html [DONE] a.jpg -> aa.jpg 2 path(s) renamed in 0.000 seconds $ tree . ├── aa.html ├── aa.jpg ├── abc │   ├── A.jpg │   ├── B.HTM │   └── B.jpg └── b.jpg 1. Renaming directories too (`-D/--including-dir`), or renaming directories only (`-D --only-dir`) $ brename -p "a" -r "A" -R -D Searching for paths to rename... Done searching. Renaming paths... [DONE] aa.html -> AA.html [DONE] aa.jpg -> AA.jpg [DONE] abc -> Abc 3 path(s) renamed in 0.001 seconds $ tree . ├── AA.html ├── AA.jpg ├── Abc │   ├── A.jpg │   ├── B.HTM │   └── B.jpg └── b.jpg 1. **Only renaming specific files via include filters (regular expression) (`-f/--include-filters`)** $ brename -p '(.)' -r ' $1' -d Searching for paths to rename... [OK] AA.html -> A A . h t m l [OK] AA.jpg -> A A . j p g [OK] b.jpg -> b . j p g 3 path(s) to be renamed $ brename -p '(.)' -r ' $1' -d -f '\.jpg$' Searching for paths to rename... [OK] AA.jpg -> A A . j p g [OK] b.jpg -> b . j p g 2 path(s) to be renamed ***Attention: values of `-f/--include-filters` and `-F/--exclude-filters` should be regular expressions, NOT wildcards!*** $ brename -p '(.)' -r '$1 ' -d -f *.jpg Seems you are using wildcard for -f/--include-filters? Make sure using regular expression: AA.jpg Searching for paths to rename... 0 path(s) to be renamed $ brename -p '(.)' -r '$1 ' -d -f '*.jpg' Are you using wildcard for -f/--include-filters? It should be regular expression: *.jpg illegal regular expression for include filter: *.jpg $ brename -p '(.)' -r '$1 ' -d -f A* Seems you are using wildcard for -f/--include-filters? Make sure using regular expression: AA.html Searching for paths to rename... 0 path(s) to be renamed 1. Excluding files via exclude filters (regular expression) (`-F/--exclude-filters`) $ brename -p '(.)' -r ' $1' -d Searching for paths to rename... [OK] AA.html -> A A . h t m l [OK] AA.jpg -> A A . j p g [OK] b.jpg -> b . j p g 3 path(s) to be renamed $ brename -p '(.)' -r ' $1' -d -F '\.html$' Searching for paths to rename... This filter step is performed before the exclude filters. The default value `^\.` is for skipping files starting with a dot, which are hidden files in Linux. Matching subdirectories are also skipped during recursive search, even without `-D`. Include filters select files and directories to rename without pruning subdirectories. Explicit search roots are searched. If you do not want to skip hidden entries, just empty it. $ brename -p xxx -r yyy -S "" 1. Replace submatches with corresponding values via a tab-delimited key-value file (`-k/--kv-file`) Each match uses its own captured key. For example, with `a` mapped to `Alpha` and `b` mapped to `Beta`, `-p '([ab])' -r '{kv}' -k kv.tsv` renames `a-b` to `Alpha-Beta`.
